units.title: Adding and Subtracting within 20
units.blurb: Count on, make ten and use doubles to add and subtract within 20.

units.title: The Equal Sign and Word Problems
units.blurb: Learn what the equal sign means, find missing numbers and solve story problems.

units.title: Tens and Ones
units.blurb: Count to 120, see two-digit numbers as tens and ones, and add within 100.

units.title: Length, Time and Data
units.blurb: Compare and measure lengths, tell time to the hour and half hour, and sort data into groups.

units.title: Shapes and Equal Shares
units.blurb: Find what makes a shape a shape, combine shapes and split them into equal parts.

topics.title: Counting On to Add
topics.short: Start at the bigger number and count up.
topics.trouble: Children count the starting number again, so 8 + 3 comes out as 10.

topics.title: Counting Back to Subtract
topics.short: Start at the total and count back.
topics.trouble: Children say the starting number as the first step back, so 9 − 3 comes out as 7.

topics.title: Facts within 10
topics.short: Add and subtract within 10 quickly and accurately.

topics.title: Adding in Any Order
topics.short: 3 + 8 and 8 + 3 have the same sum.

topics.title: Doubles and Near Doubles
topics.short: 6 + 7 is 6 + 6 and one more.

topics.title: Making Ten to Add
topics.trouble: Children break the second number apart the wrong way, so 8 + 5 becomes 10 + 5.

topics.title: Subtraction as a Missing Addend
topics.short: To find 13 − 8, think 8 plus what makes 13.

topics.title: Facts within 20
topics.short: Choose a strategy to add or subtract within 20.

topics.title: Adding Three Numbers
topics.short: Look for a pair that makes 10 or a double first.

topics.title: The Equal Sign Means "Same Amount"
topics.short: Both sides of = name the same amount.
topics.trouble: Children read = as "the answer comes next," so they call 7 = 3 + 4 false or fill in 9 for 3 + 6 = ? + 3.

topics.title: True or False?
topics.short: Decide whether both sides of an equation are equal.

topics.title: Finding the Missing Number
topics.short: Find the unknown in 8 + ? = 11 or 14 − ? = 9.
topics.trouble: Children add the two numbers they can see, writing 19 in 8 + ? = 11.

topics.title: Add To and Take From Stories
topics.short: Solve stories where something joins or leaves a group.

topics.title: Put Together and Take Apart Stories
topics.short: Solve stories about two parts and a whole.

topics.title: How Many More? How Many Fewer?
topics.short: Solve stories that compare two amounts.
topics.trouble: Children see the word "more" and add, even when the story asks how many more one has than the other.

topics.title: Counting and Writing to 120
topics.short: Count, read and write numbers up to 120.
topics.trouble: After 109, children write 1010 for one hundred ten, writing the parts they hear.

topics.title: Tens and Ones
topics.short: 47 is 4 tens and 7 ones.
topics.trouble: Children think the 4 in 47 means 4, not 4 tens.

topics.title: Counting by Tens
topics.short: 10, 20, 30 … 90 are 1 ten, 2 tens … 9 tens.

topics.title: Comparing Two-Digit Numbers
topics.short: Compare the tens first, then the ones, and use <, = and >.
topics.trouble: Children compare the ones digits first and say 29 > 31, or mix up the < and > symbols.

topics.title: 10 More and 10 Less
topics.short: Change the tens digit by one without counting.
topics.trouble: Children change the ones digit, so 10 more than 34 becomes 35.

topics.title: Adding Tens
topics.short: Add a multiple of 10 to a two-digit number, like 34 + 20.

topics.title: Adding Ones to a Two-Digit Number
topics.short: Add tens to tens and ones to ones.
topics.trouble: Children add a one-digit number to the tens, so 42 + 5 becomes 92.

topics.title: Adding That Makes a New Ten
topics.short: 27 + 6: the ones make a new ten.
topics.trouble: Children write 213 for 27 + 6, putting the 13 ones next to the 2 tens.

topics.title: Subtracting Tens
topics.short: Subtract multiples of 10, like 70 − 30.

topics.title: Ordering by Length
topics.short: Compare two things by comparing each to a third.

topics.title: Measuring with Same-Size Units
topics.short: Lay units end to end with no gaps or overlaps.
topics.trouble: Children leave gaps or overlap the units, or use units of different sizes in one measurement.

topics.title: Time to the Hour and Half Hour
topics.short: Read and write times like 3:00 and 3:30.
topics.trouble: At half past, children read the hour hand as the next hour, saying 4:30 is 5:30.

topics.title: Data in Three Groups
topics.short: Organize data and answer how many more or fewer.

topics.title: What Makes a Shape a Shape
topics.short: Sides and corners matter; color, size and turning do not.
topics.trouble: Children think a big red triangle and a small blue one are different kinds of shapes.

topics.title: Putting Shapes Together
topics.short: Combine shapes to make new shapes.

topics.title: Halves and Fourths
topics.short: Split circles and rectangles into 2 or 4 equal parts.
topics.trouble: Children think more parts means bigger parts, so a fourth is bigger than a half.
